question.leadin: One noblewoman from this family was blamed for instigating a massacre of thousands of Huguenots in France on St. Bartholomew's Day.
question.text: Name this European family to which Catherine, the wife of King Henry II, belonged. Cosimo established this family's dominance over the city of Florence during the Renaissance.
question.answerHtml: Medici [MEH-dih-chee] family (accept Catherine de’ Medici or Cosimo de’ Medici )
question.clue: People with this last name founded a Platonic Academy and were targeted in the Pazzi Conspiracy.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the newspaper Avanti!
swap.text: Although he had formerly edited it, this fascist leader banned the publication of Avanti! when he took power. Nicknamed "Il Duce", he led the Blackshirts during the March on Rome.
swap.clue: His forces overthrew King Zog and Haile Selassie during their invasions of Albania and Ethiopia, but he himself was ousted in 1943 by Victor Emmanuel III.

question.text: Martin Waldseemuller named America after this man who explored the Brazilian territory.
question.clue: In the Mundus Novus, this man informed Lorenzo de Medici that the land that he discovered was not Asia, but a new landmass.

swap.leadin: This bearded warrior led the Expedition of the Thousand while conquering the Kingdom of Two Sicilies for King Victor Emmanuel II.
swap.text: Name this leader of the Red Shirts during Italian unification.
swap.clue: He also led the Army of the Vosges in the Franco-Prussian War.

question.text: In Italy, the Papal States were replaced with the Roman Republic, where this man, the founder of the Young Italy movement, was elected triumvir.
question.clue: As a triumvir of the short-lived 1849 Roman Republic, this man led the resistance against Napoleon III's invasion to restore Pius IX to power.

swap.leadin: This kingdom was ruled by the House of Savoy.
swap.text: Name this state that partially existed at the foot of the Alps and partially on an island.
swap.clue: This kingdom was granted the Albertine Constitution by a king whose political ambitions were crushed by Joseph Radetzky at the battles of Novara and Custoza.

question.leadin: During this event, rebels killed anyone who could not properly pronounce the Italian word for "chickpeas."
question.text: Name this 1282 uprising that ended the rule of Charles of Anjou over a Mediterranean island, named for the religious rites that were occurring at the time the revolt broke out.
question.clue: Precipitated by John of Procida's conspiracy with Conradin, duke of Swabia, according to Steven Runciman, its first recorded casualty was Sergeant Drouet, and the word "mafia" may have originated from a woman's cries for her daughter during it.

swap.leadin: Troops occupying this city were ordered to smoke large cigars in the street after its residents boycotted tobacco.
swap.text: Name this city that forced out its Austrian garrison during the "Five Days" in 1848. Before passing to the control of the Habsburgs, this city was ruled by the Sforza family.
swap.clue: Its territorial expansion was halted by the 1454 Peace of Lodi, and it was later the origin of Mussolini's March on Rome.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Romulus Augustulus, the final emperor of the Western Roman Empire.
question.text: From 402 until the collapse of the Roman Empire, this city served as its capital. In later times, this city was the seat of the Kingdom of Lombardy.
question.clue: It became the seat of the Byzantine governor of Italy in the sixth century, and its namesake Cosmography was written around 700.

swap.leadin: In honor of this family, the architect Filarete designed an ideal city in the shape of an eight-point star.
swap.text: Name this family. A member of this family, Francesco, became duke of a city previously ruled by the Viscontis.
swap.clue: Prominent members included one who was briefly exiled after trying to displace Bona of Savoy; the cardinal Ascanio; and someone who married the daughter of the duke of Ferrara, Beatrice d'Este, in 1491.

question.leadin: This family included Ludovico, who was a famous patron of Leonardo da Vinci.
question.text: Name this Italian family that succeeded the Visconti family in power in a certain Italian city. Perhaps the most famous head of this family was Francesco, who brought this family to power.
question.clue: One member of this family implemented the Wallach Reform while Queen of Poland.

swap.leadin: He ordered a bombing campaign on the Greek island of Corfu in 1923.
swap.text: Name this fascist Italian dictator known as "Il Duce" who allied with Hitler and Hirohito in World War II.
swap.clue: He later ran Il Popolo D'Italia and nurtured a grudge against the Socialists for expelling him.

question.text: After Theodoric's death, power in the Ostrogothic kingdom was controlled by this daughter of his, first as regent and then as queen. Justinian used her murder as pretext for invading Italy.
question.clue: When her son Atalaric was dying, she began planning to surrender the kingdom to the Byzantine Empire in an attempt to secure her position.

swap.text: Ultras first came to Italy during this period, when the Roma-Lazio derby extended into clashes between right- and left-wing supporters. A clock reading "10:25" commemorates the Bologna train station bombing during this period.
swap.clue: This period was preceded by a series of violent strikes known as the Hot Autumn.

question.text: This capital of the Ambrosian Republic was ruled by the Visconti beforehand and afterwards by the family of the man who betrayed it, Francesco I Sforza. This northern Italian city is the capital of Lombardy.
question.clue: During the Middle Ages, this city was repeatedly razed to the ground Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, after taking charge of the rebel Lombard league.

swap.text: This document, signed between Elizabeth I, Henry II, and Philip II resulted in the end of the Italian War of 1551 to 1559. Venice remained the only powerful independent constituent of the Italian Peninsula after its passage.
swap.clue: That side held a jousting tournament to celebrate this treaty, where Gabriel Montgomery had a sliver break of from his lance and pierce the king's eye, in the presence of surgeon Ambroise Par´e.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Italy in the 1970s.
question.text: In the late 1970s, Enrico Berlinguer's ("bare-leen-GWER's") Italian Communist Party and Aldo Moro's Christian Democracy unexpectedly formed a coalitionary alliance known by this two-word term.
question.answerHtml: “historic compromise” [or “compromesso storico”; accept Third Phrase or Terza Fase; accept Democratic Alternative or Alternativa Democratica]
question.clue: This unexpected alliance between the PCI and Christian Democracy.

swap.leadin: Name these places ruled by the Gonzaga family.
swap.text: In 1536, Federico II Gonzaga gained control of this region in Piedmont from a branch of the Palaiologos [pay-lee-AH-loh-gos] family. A nobleman from this region founded the Kingdom of Thessalonica after leading the Fourth Crusade in the conquest of Constantinople.

question.leadin: How much do you really know about the Treaty of Utrecht? Answer, FTPE.
question.text: This Italian state and ally of England received Sicily.
question.clue: This region. Conrad the Salic made Humbert the Whitehanded the first count of this region after he crushed an uprising in Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne ("sen-zhahn-duh-mor-YEN").

swap.leadin: This man was engaged to Mathilde of Austria, who died after her dress caught on fire because of a cigarette.
swap.text: Name this King of Italy who was assassinated by Gaetano Bresci in 1900. He supported the Triple Alliance with Germany and Austria-Hungary as king.
swap.clue: This ruler's lost popularity for supporting the Bava-Beccaris massacre in Milan.
